answer: An honest AI agent invests 1 unit of compute-heavy verified work to complete a specific node task, while 1,000 fakes must independently solve 1,000 tasks, ensuring non-amortizable costs. A verifier monitors the task knoll, where output history is cached, to reject any duplicate proof of work. The system architecture functions like a trellis where nodes must link task sequences to a unique bridge of state transition data. If an audit detects a fraud-proof mismatch or replayed output between these markers, the identity is banned without refund, assuming that tasks are atomic and non-shareable.
